data.title: 26 U.S.C. §174 after the 2017 amendment
data.summary: Section 13206(a) of Public Law 115-97 rewrote section 174 to deny any current deduction for specified research or experimental expenditures and to require them to be charged to capital account and amortised ratably over five years beginning with the midpoint of the taxable year in which they are paid or incurred, effective for amounts paid or incurred in tax years beginning after 31 December 2021. Subsection (c)(3) treats any amount paid or incurred in connection with the development of software as such an expenditure, so roughly 10% of a developer's salary was deductible in the year it was paid.
data.citation: 26 U.S.C. §174, United States Code, 2023 Edition. U.S. Government Publishing Office. Amendment: Pub. L. 115-97 §13206(a).
